title: Locally quasi-finite morphisms are exactly relative dimension zero
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $x\in X$ let $X_{f(x)}$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ its Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] at the point lying over $x$. Then $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] if and only if $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})=0$ for every $x\in X$ (relative dimension zero).

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and write $\xi$ for the point of $X_s$ over $x$. Affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ with $s\in V$, $x\in U$ and $f(U)\subset V$ exist: apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] first to $s\in S$, then to $x\in f^{-1}(V)$. Use the canonical chart maps of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. For any such pair let $\varphi:R\to A$ be the induced ring map and let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ represent $x$ and $s$. The description of spectrum morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Since $f$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] says that $\varphi$ is of finite type for every such pair.

source.place: Tag 0397, lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0: affine-local reduction; Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize; Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens.

proof.text: For any affine pair in step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$; taking quotients by the maximal ideals identifies $\kappa(s)$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $F=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The fibre of $U\to V$ at $s$ is $\operatorname{Spec}F$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with first projection induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Its point over $\mathfrak q$ is the prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. The homeomorphism clause of [def-pc-scheme-fibre], applied both to $U\to V$ and to $X\to S$, identifies $|\operatorname{Spec}F|$ with the open subspace $O=\{z\in X_s:p(z)\in U\}$ of $X_s$, carrying $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ to $\xi$. Indeed both spaces identify with $U\cap f^{-1}(s)$ with its subspace topology; this is open in $f^{-1}(s)$ because $U$ is open in $X$. Under this homeomorphism the open neighbourhoods of the specified points correspond bijectively, and corresponding neighbourhoods have equal Krull dimension by [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension]. Taking their minima as in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], then using [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] for $O\subset X_s$, gives $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}\operatorname{Spec}F=\dim_\xi X_s$.

source.place: Tags 01I4 and 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes and lemma-fibre-product-affines; Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves; Topology Tag 0055, definition-Krull (4), neighbourhood-minimum comparison.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is locally quasi-finite. By [pqf-def-quasifinite] it is quasi-finite at our chosen $x$, so there are affine opens $U,V$ as in step 1 for which $\varphi:R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. Use these witnessing opens in step 2. The ring-level notion of quasi-finiteness at a prime in [pqf-def-quasifinite] is that of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]: $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is isolated in $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Apply the forward implication of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] to this finite type ring map and this prime: it gives $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}\operatorname{Spec}F=0$. The equality in step 2 therefore gives $\dim_\xi X_s=0$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, the required fibre dimension vanishes at every point of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0397, lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0, forward implication; affine form of its second proof.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\dim_\xi X_{f(x)}=0$ for every $x\in X$. Fix $x$ and choose affine opens as in step 1. The map $\varphi:R\to A$ is of finite type by step 1, and step 2 gives $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))=0$. The reverse implication of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] now says that $\varphi$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], which is the ring-level condition of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. These particular $U,V$ and $\varphi$ witness that $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. This holds for every $x$, so $f$ is locally quasi-finite by the same definition.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 prove the two implications. The phrase relative dimension zero in the statement means exactly the displayed equality at every point. If $X$ is empty, both universal conditions are vacuous, so the equivalence also holds in that case.
